SET8 Y334 is a conserved residue that is critical for the regulation of its product specificity through altering its active-site water affinity, and that the Phe-Tyr switch is a key regulatory mechanism in SET domain methyltransferases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Phe switch of SET8 is a key determinant for the enzyme to catalyze monomethylation and the Tyr switch is a determinant for dimethylation.
the structural origins for the product-specificity switch in SET domain protein methyl transferases (PKMT) are revealed through structural and biochemical analysis of a SET8 mutant.
the structural basis for product specificity is that the phenyl ring of the Phe/Ty switch in the SET domain of PKMTs forms a hydrophobic pocket for the lysine substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Phe switch in SET8 regulates the product specificity of the enzyme by altering the binding affinity of a water molecule in the active site.
the structural basis for the product specificity switch in SET8, and likely other SET domain proteins, is the modulation of an active site water molecule.

the Phe switch, which is conserved across all SET domain protein lysyl methyltransferases, is not only important for the catalysis of the methyl transfer reaction, but it is also critical for the specificity of the reaction.
